hero.lede: Tony Yanick is an artist, educator, and computational media researcher working across film/video, sound, installation, generative systems, and participatory media environments. His work investigates how technological infrastructures, speculative narratives, and audiovisual systems shape perception, collective desire, and lived experience through unstable relationships between image, signal, memory, and space.

works.title: Works investigating how image, sound, computation, infrastructure, and fiction organize perception, memory, participation, and collective experience.

statement.title: My work operates through fiction—not as representation, but as a force that produces conditions.
paragraphs: I am interested in how narrative, myth, mediated images, and technological systems organize collective desire, and how these structures persist, circulate, and mutate across media environments.

The work develops across film, sound, installation, performance, and computational media—not as movement between disciplines, but as interference between forms. Image, sound, code, archives, and spatial systems interact to produce unstable relationships between perception, atmosphere, participation, and interpretation.

Rather than constructing fixed narratives, these works build environments that audiences enter, navigate, and activate through participation and duration. Installations and audiovisual systems often unfold through projected image, fragmented archives, distorted voice, live transmission, feedback systems, and accumulated audiovisual residue.

I return repeatedly to temporal displacement. Fragments of possible worlds appear out of sequence—past events reconfigured as future projections, speculative structures embedded within existing archives, signals that arrive too early or too late. These works accumulate through repetition, drift, and recursion, allowing fiction to operate not as storytelling alone, but as an active condition shaping perception and experience.

Sound functions as an affective force before interpretation stabilizes, producing atmospheres of instability, delay, and pressure. Images are not treated as fixed objects, but as contingent forms shaped by the conditions under which they are encountered.

Computational systems extend this condition. I engage generative and networked media not simply as tools for production, but as infrastructures that compress, redistribute, and reorganize perception. Works such as Artificial Cinema, N2: The Secretary, HYPNAGNOSIS, TRANSMISSIONS, and COSMOMORPHOSIS operate as layered configurations of language, signal, sound, image, and live systems—environments that can be entered, but never fully resolved.

Archives—both real and fictional—are treated as material. Documents, recordings, found media, synthetic images, and historical traces are recombined into unstable configurations that blur distinctions between memory, projection, simulation, and evidence.

Collaboration operates as another layer within this structure. Performers, participants, audiences, and systems interact to produce outcomes that cannot emerge through isolated authorship alone. These works often evolve through accumulation, interference, and collective activation, allowing perception to shift as elements overlap, repeat, and destabilize one another.
There is no stable image at the end of this process—only signals that continue to circulate.

research.title: Researching computational media as operative environments whose internal conditions can be examined, altered, and reorganized through intervention.

cards.title: Limits of CTRL
cards.text: Limits of CTRL: Neural Bending and the Generic Machine reframes trained generative models as computational media architectures that organize relational possibility rather than systems that simply produce representations or execute commands. The project investigates how coherence emerges through distributed operations including embedding, attention, normalization, temporal propagation, and infrastructural execution.

cards.title: Neural bending
cards.text: Neural bending is developed as a research-creation method for experimentally intervening within generative systems through controlled architectural perturbation. Rather than optimizing outputs, the method modifies embedding relations, attention distributions, normalization behavior, temporal propagation, and execution conditions in order to observe how generative coherence reorganizes under constraint.

cards.title: Operative media theory
cards.text: The research extends media-theoretical inquiry into the architectural interior of contemporary machine learning systems by treating trained models as operative media environments rather than opaque technical tools. Computational systems are approached as metastable infrastructures that shape articulation, visibility, coherence, memory, and perception through distributed internal operations.

cards.title: Research-creation environments
cards.text: These investigations extend into installations, live audiovisual systems, speculative broadcasts, generative environments, and computational media works including Artificial Cinema, TRANSMISSIONS, COSMOMORPHOSIS, and PODKOP. Across these projects, image, sound, code, archives, and live systems operate as interconnected environments shaped through instability, recursion, participation, and temporal drift.

cards.title: Fiction as operational structure
cards.text: Another axis of the research examines fiction not as narrative content alone, but as an operational structure embedded within technical and social systems. Through speculative and design-fiction methodologies, distributed environments emerge in which meaning is produced through interfaces, archives, signals, protocols, participation, and generative processes.

cards.title: Distributed perception and infrastructure
cards.text: The broader research examines how computational, audiovisual, and infrastructural systems organize collective perception and social experience. Rather than treating media as neutral channels of representation, the work approaches technical systems as active environments through which perception, participation, memory, and collective meaning are continuously reorganized.

teaching.title: Teaching across media systems, computation, audiovisual practice, and speculative world-building.
teaching.intro: My teaching approaches media—analog, digital, networked, and computational—not as isolated disciplines, but as interconnected systems that shape perception, behavior, participation, and collective experience. Courses are structured as collaborative environments where students develop technical, conceptual, and critical frameworks through experimentation, production, discussion, and iterative research across sound, moving image, computation, installation, writing, and hybrid media practices.

materials.title: Programming for Digital Art
materials.text: Designed and taught a studio-based course integrating computational media, audiovisual systems, code, generative processes, and conceptual frameworks. Students developed interdisciplinary projects spanning sound, video, interaction, installation, and hybrid media environments.

materials.title: Fictional Worlds / Possible Futures: Building Conditions
materials.text: A collaborative world-building studio approaching fiction as the construction of shared conditions rather than narrative alone. Students developed evolving systems through archives, platforms, spatial structures, performance, distributed media, and participatory activation models.

materials.title: Machines, Codes and Cultures
materials.text: Facilitated discussions connecting media technologies, computational systems, and network culture to historical, theoretical, and political contexts while supporting students in critically analyzing media infrastructures and digital culture.

materials.title: World Cinema
materials.text: Supported students in analyzing cinematic language, spectatorship, historical film movements, and global moving-image traditions through screening analysis, discussion, and critical writing.

materials.title: Semiotics and Media Interpretation
materials.type: Case Western Reserve University · Teaching Assistant
materials.text: Introduced students to frameworks for analyzing language, meaning, representation, textual systems, and visual culture across philosophy, media, and communication practices.

materials.title: The New Centre for Research & Practice
materials.text: Developed interdisciplinary courses integrating philosophy, art, technology, computation, and experimental media within a globally distributed learning environment. Mentored students across artistic, technical, and theoretical practices through collaborative and research-driven pedagogical models.

materials.title: NewBridge Cleveland
materials.text: Designed and facilitated arts education programs for youth and community participants, emphasizing experimentation, accessibility, collaboration, and creative confidence through interdisciplinary media practices.

projects.title: ARTIFICIAL CINEMA
projects.question: What does a machine see when it 'watches' science fiction films?
projects.summary: A collaborative investigation into how cinematic perception changes when processed through machine logic.
projects.system: Artificial Cinema explored science fiction cinema not as narrative, but as a computational dataset composed of image data, motion, texture, rhythm, and temporal structure. Developed through custom-built algorithmic systems, the project reorganized cinematic material through machine vision, semantic analysis, and generative montage. Rather than presenting a fixed film, the installation operated as a continuously evolving audiovisual environment shaped through interaction between human subjectivity and computational perception.

projects.title: PODKOP
projects.context: Strelka Institute / The New Normal Residency
projects.question: How can language, infrastructure, and AI converge into city-scale narrative systems?
projects.summary: An urban-scale AI system generating and distributing interactive fictions across the city through live infrastructure and participatory interaction.
projects.system: PODKOP processes environmental data, movement patterns, infrastructural signals, and archival material through generative language systems trained on historical, cosmological, and philosophical texts. Operating through a Telegram-based interface embedded within urban space, the project functions simultaneously as fiction engine, navigational system, and participatory infrastructure.
projects.embed: Urban fiction system / Telegram interface documentation

projects.title: TRANSMISSIONS
projects.question: What if a signal doesn’t represent reality, but begins to produce it?
projects.summary: An evolving transmission environment combining spoken word, sound, distributed media, speculative fiction, and signal drift into a fragmented broadcast infrastructure.
projects.system: Created in collaboration with Messiah in Glytch, TRANSMISSIONS operates as a distributed signal rather than a single work. Audio broadcasts emerge as transmissions from a speculative near-future world, leaking into the present through distortion, delay, recursion, and signal contamination. Fragments function simultaneously as archive and forecast, documenting and producing possible worlds at the same time.

projects.title: HYPNAGNOSIS
projects.question: How can altered sleep-wake states become a shared visual system?
projects.summary: An ongoing multimedia project combining risograph print, collage, drawing, sound, installation, and moving image to investigate hypnagogic hallucination, sleep paralysis, lucid dreaming, and altered temporal states.
projects.system: Beginning from lived experience, HYPNAGNOSIS explores states where waking and dreaming collapse into one another, producing layered, delayed, and unstable perceptual conditions. Through cut-up collage, overprint, montage, symbolic repetition, occult diagrams, and fragmented image systems, the project constructs a visual language for experiences that resist ordinary description.

projects.title: COSMOMORPHOSIS
projects.question: How can data operate as pressure rather than representation?
projects.summary: An evolving audiovisual installation driven by live telemetry from the International Space Station.
projects.system: Rather than visualizing data directly, COSMOMORPHOSIS reroutes orbital information—position, velocity, electromagnetic fluctuation, and drift—into the procedural behavior of the image itself. Motion, rupture, decay, and transformation emerge through the continual pressure of real orbital conditions acting upon a generative audiovisual structure.

projects.title: Dossier 37
projects.question: How do signals become geopolitical narratives?
projects.format: Audiovisual work, forensic interface, data visualization
projects.summary: An audiovisual work developed in collaboration with AUDINT investigating sonic warfare discourse, disinformation systems, and perceptual instability.
projects.system: Emerging from discourse surrounding alleged sonic attacks on US diplomatic personnel in Cuba and South China, the project examines how fear, rumor, and signal interpretation circulate through contemporary media systems. Structured through forensic interface aesthetics, Twitter visualization, speculative timelines, and audiovisual reconstruction, the work treats evidence itself as unstable media terrain.

projects.title: Flow Lines (3-channel video)
projects.question: How do landscapes carry memory, migration, and historical movement?
projects.summary: A collaborative installation exploring migration, geography, historical memory, and movement through the Niagara River region.
projects.system: Developed in response to Isaac Julien’s Kapital, the project approaches the Niagara River simultaneously as landscape, historical boundary, and infrastructural flow system connected to the Underground Railroad. Through layered moving image, rhythm, and spoken language, the installation constructs landscape as an active carrier of memory and movement.

projects.title: BOBBI LYNN
projects.question: What happens when memory is reconstructed through machine vision?
projects.summary: A music video exploring grief, intimacy, and memory through generative image systems and synthetic reconstruction.
projects.system: Centered on recollections of familial relationships, the work replaces direct photographic reconstruction with unstable synthetic imagery generated through machine-learning systems. Memory becomes probabilistic, fragmented, and continuously reassembled through computational mediation.

projects.title: surFACE
projects.question: How can repetitive drawing become unstable audiovisual material?
projects.format: Short film, analog recording systems, tape-based process
projects.summary: A short film investigating analog recording systems, repetitive drawing, feedback, and audiovisual instability.
projects.system: Constructed through iterative drawing, recording, playback, degradation, layering, and analog transformation, surFACE treats marks as unstable audiovisual material rather than static representation. Image and sound evolve together through recursive recording behavior and feedback structures.
projects.embed: Analog feedback film / recording system documentation

projects.title: The Fixers: Naudia Loftis
projects.question: How can documentary operate through collaboration rather than extraction?
projects.summary: A collaborative documentary centered on Naudia Loftis and community organizing in Cleveland’s Kinsman neighborhood during the 2016 Republican National Convention.
projects.system: Built through interviews, collaboration, and community participation, the film foregrounds lived experience within conditions shaped by systemic violence, displacement, and political instability. The project prioritizes proximity, dialogue, and collective authorship over imposed narrative structure.

projects.title: Make America Great Again ... And Again
projects.question: How does political language reorganize collective perception?
projects.summary: An experimental video work drawing on Octavia E. Butler’s Parable trilogy to examine political language, mediated desire, and speculative power.
projects.system: Through montage, abstraction, recursive slogan structures, and layered media fragments, the project investigates how political narratives circulate as systems of emotional management, identity construction, and social control.
